heading: 25 October 2026 — paired TRAIN labels: variation exists, economic coherence untested
body:
25 October 2026 — paired TRAIN labels: variation exists, economic coherence untested
A metadata-first audit and the subsequent frozen FIT-only target audit are complete. The fixed cohort contains 80 declared FIT timetable groups: 79 source0/source1 pairs and one source1-only group, physical_v2_s10037. All 80 stored case identities and all 159 source-market and whole-plan identities matched their pinned TRAIN tables. This is stored identity/membership consistency, not independent physical replay or teacher optimality. The two tables contain mixed TRAIN partitions: all bytes were hashed once and rows transiently JSON-decoded for routing; non-FIT rows were immediately discarded without semantic analysis. No sealed bank, historical outer performance, model weights, solver or fitting was accessed.
Among the 79 admitted pairs, 48 have different selected-movement targets and 31 are identical. The same 48/31 split holds for flexible direct/depot choices. Vehicle counts are equal within every pair. The source-market identities bind different linear tariffs on the common physical grid and equal curvature b=1/900. These observations resolve whether this stored FIT substrate ever supplies different membership targets across source-price contexts: it does. They do not identify tariff causality, predictable information or the quality of the teacher choices. Exact historical GNN pool lineage remains unverified; the audited pool is explicitly pinned by CatBoost preprocessing and matches the groups declared by both preprocessors.
For flexible modes, median Hamming disagreement is 1/160, or 0.625% of all candidate flexible modes. Median disagreement relative to the positive union is 2/13, about 15.38%. Both metrics are defined in all 79 pairs and include the 31 identical pairs. These are group-level medians with different denominators, not accuracy, average bill savings or independent edge observations. The small candidate-universe fraction motivates examining target weighting and economic relevance; it does not establish that a ranking loss would improve decisions.
The labels are membership in one observed feasible-incumbent schedule, not certified optimal alternatives. Different targets may reflect price response, teacher search, initialization, unequal incumbent quality, or a mixture. Same fleet count removes a fleet-number explanation here but leaves routing, energy and charging differences. Before refitting, the next proposed diagnostic will independently replay the two unchanged witnesses and cross-value each whole schedule at both source tariffs under c+a'L+0.5L'BL. It will distinguish preference reversals, ties and own-context choices dominated by the other observed witness. That is a two-witness catalog consistency check, not global optimality, optimized fixed-route charging, a new theorem or learned-price-information value. Exact replay fields, tolerances, sources, command and budget still require a prospective freeze. The completed warm study's failed 1%E0 learned-increment gate remains unchanged.
